newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ups pressure in World Cup soccer stadium row.
newsitem.headline: EU ups pressure in World Cup soccer stadium row.

text.p: The European Commission began court action on Thursday to resolve its legal battle with France over the award of contracts to build and run the country's flagship stadium in Paris for the 1998 World Cup soccer finals.
"The Commission has decided to refer France to the Court of Justice for violation of the directive on public procurement of construction works..." the EU executive said in a statement.

Months of legal wrangling between Brussels and Paris have failed to resolve questions about equal treatment of bidders and the award of operating concessions for the 80,000-seater "Grand Stade de France" in the Saint Denis suburb.

"The contracting authority's attitude contradicts the fundamental principle of equal treatment on which the EU's public procurement rules are based," EU Single Market Commissioner Mario Monti said in the statement.
"The equal treatement principle is essential for ensuring contracts are awarded transparently and objectively and for maintaining legal certainty for tenderers," Monti added.
The Commission also wants to know why the construction contract was granted not for building the stadium but for operating it, a matter it says raises subsidy questions.

Commission inquiries date from October 1995, after competing companies cried foul over the award of contracts, accusing successful bidders Bouyges, Dumez and SGE of having changed their bid after its submission.
The 2.67-billion-franc ($458 million) stadium, now largely built and dominating the northern road routes into the French capital, is due for completion in November this year. ($=5.82 francs)
